findings.evidence: "Also, the stipend request, once the manager signs it, after finance confirms the budget line, moves to final processing."
findings.fix: Restructure as: "Once the manager signs the request and finance confirms the budget line, the stipend request moves to final processing."
findings.location: How to Apply section, second paragraph
findings.violation: The sentence structure makes the sequence of approvals unclear - it's ambiguous whether the manager signs before or after finance confirms the budget line.

findings.evidence: "The employee receives a confirmation email once processing finishes. Then, the employee reviews the confirmation summary before submitting the final request."
findings.fix: Reorder these sentences so the employee reviews the summary before submitting, and only receives confirmation after processing completes.
findings.location: How to Apply section, third paragraph
findings.violation: The workflow described is logically backwards - the employee is shown reviewing and submitting after processing has already finished.

findings.evidence: "A photo of the receipt is enough for most requests."
findings.fix: Specify conditions clearly, such as "A photo of the receipt is sufficient for requests under $250" or remove "most" to apply the policy uniformly.
findings.violation: The statement is vague about which requests require a physical receipt versus a photo, leaving unclear guidance for edge cases.

findings.evidence: "The finance office deposits the amount within one pay cycle."
findings.fix: Clarify as "The finance office deposits the approved reimbursement within one pay cycle."
findings.violation: It is ambiguous whether "the amount" refers to the full $500 stipend or only the approved/reimbursable portion.

findings.evidence: "You must keep your equipment in good working condition and we may ask for a brief photo check once a year."
findings.fix: Rewrite as "Employees must keep equipment in good working condition. The benefits team may request a photo verification once a year."
findings.location: Restrictions and Exceptions section, first paragraph
findings.violation: Pronouns shift to second person (you/we) while the rest of the document uses third person (employees/benefits team), creating tone inconsistency.

findings.evidence: "Similarly, the policy applies to one device per category per employee."
findings.fix: Replace "Similarly" with "Additionally" or restructure without a transition word.
findings.location: Restrictions and Exceptions section, second paragraph
findings.violation: The transition word "Similarly" does not logically connect to the preceding sentence about equipment maintenance.

findings.evidence: Section titled "Terminology Notes" contains "You record the stipend item on the request form. Finance reconciles the reimbursable item against the request log each month."
findings.fix: Rename the section to "Request Processing" or "Workflow Steps."
findings.location: Terminology Notes section, heading and content
findings.violation: The section does not define terminology; it describes workflow processes, making the heading misleading.

findings.evidence: "You record the stipend item on the request form. Finance reconciles the reimbursable item against the request log each month. Also, you submit the request in the portal. Countersign the employee request within two business days. You track its status there until the payment clears."
findings.fix: Clarify roles explicitly, e.g., "The employee records the stipend item and submits the request. The manager countersigns within two business days. The employee tracks the status in the portal."
findings.violation: Unclear who "you" refers to and which roles perform which actions; "Countersign" implies a different actor but the pronoun switches back to "you."

findings.evidence: "Completing the request begins with confirming eligibility, and the uploaded receipt."
findings.fix: Rewrite as "Completing the request requires confirming eligibility and uploading a receipt" or list as separate ordered steps.
findings.violation: The sentence structure is incomplete and has a broken parallel construction.

findings.evidence: "The IT asset group updates the equipment catalog after every open enrollment period. Every entry carries a date stamp so the record stays easy to audit."
findings.fix: Remove this duplicate or consolidate related information into a single section.
findings.violation: This statement is verbatim repetition of content from the Program Overview section.

findings.evidence: "A separate audit last spring reviewed unrelated travel expenses. Federal guidance on remote work continues to evolve each year. The office coffee budget was reset at the start of the quarter."
findings.fix: Delete these sentences; they do not belong in this document.
findings.violation: These three sentences are unrelated to the home-office equipment stipend policy and appear out of place.

findings.evidence: "The most recent version supersedes the one that came before it."
findings.fix: Remove this duplicate statement or consolidate the sections.
